title: Add jit-planning-lead scenario evals for its entry paths
description:
Give jit-planning-lead its own `evals/` directory with scenario evals covering each of its documented entry paths, run and graded under the same adjudication method used for jit-execution-lead's evals.

## Background

jit-planning-lead has no `evals/` directory. Its SKILL.md documents three entry paths for starting a planning session: research-and-plan (only a vague idea to refine), plan-from-existing (a container already has success criteria to seed a plan from), and plan-from-import (an external planning document to reconcile). None of these paths has ever been exercised by a scenario eval.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `.claude/skills/jit-planning-lead/evals/evals.json` defines at least one scenario eval for each of the three entry paths (research-and-plan, plan-from-existing, plan-from-import), each with a prompt, a setup scenario, and an `expected_output` rubric grounded in what that entry path actually produces, following the same schema as jit-execution-lead's `evals/evals.json`.
- [hard] REQ-02: `.claude/skills/jit-planning-lead/evals/` contains the setup script(s) needed to stand up a fresh test repository for each scenario before it runs.
- [hard] REQ-03: Every scenario defined in `.claude/skills/jit-planning-lead/evals/evals.json` has been run at least once and graded using the documented scenario-eval adjudication method.
- [hard] REQ-04: `.claude/skills/jit-planning-lead/evals/results.md` records a passing verdict for every scenario, with the transcript location or completed checklist backing each verdict.

## Notes

Ground each scenario's `expected_output` in what the entry path's SKILL.md step actually produces (a container issue with criteria, a completed plan and breakdown, or a reconciled import) rather than paraphrasing the request that triggers it.
